content:
Hi friends!

I've been a huge fan of the Lean4 ecosystem for a while, love all the work you're doing!
In the spirit of the recent push for cybersecurity, especially by anthropic -

I'm posting this fun side project I've done during this weekend - a proof of concept for auditing any constant's dependencies to the leaf axioms/opaques/externs and even tracing the C source code of an external symbol from the build artifacts.
In this project, we walk any constant's transitive dependencies through 2 passes of analysis and flag:

  • Non-standard axiom usage for dismissing proof obligations
  • Extern FFI bindings that escape into native code
  • Attempts to follow the extern symbols back to their original C source implementation, compare the declared Lean4 type to the expected C source type, and flag lack of finding and/or mismatch

Github link: https://github.com/levzlotnik/lean4-dep-audit

Here's what the output looks like when it finds a type mismatch between a Lean declaration and its C implementation:

findings:
  - name: FfiFixture.ffiWrongRet
    kind: extern "test_ffi_wrong_ret"
    type: "UInt32 → UInt32"
    provenance: traced ".../ffi.c:33"
    type-check: MISMATCH return type: expected uint32_t, got uint8_t
    expected-c-sig: "uint32_t test_ffi_wrong_ret(uint32_t)"
    actual-c-sig: "uint8_t test_ffi_wrong_ret(uint32_t)"

And when everything matches:

  - name: FfiFixture.ffiAdd
    kind: extern "test_ffi_add"
    type: "UInt32 → UInt32 → UInt32"
    provenance: traced ".../ffi.c:13"
    type-check: compatible

Full transparency: Claude Opus 4.6 was a major contributor - I leaned on it heavily throughout. Sharing because I think the concept is useful regardless, and I'd love feedback on the approach!

Lev Zlotnik said:

  • Attempts to follow the extern symbols back to their original C source implementation, compare the declared Lean4 type to the expected C source type, and flag lack of finding and/or mismatch

This is great to have, but I'd argue that this is covering for a missing feature in the lean compiler; it should output header files so that the C compiler can tell the user that the header and call site don't match!

I'm down to contributing it to the lean compiler, if that's something people would be interested in! I'm new in this community, I'm still getting the hang of the process. Would appreciate pointers (pun intended)!

One of the use cases I was thinking of for tracing back to C source code was about auditing how external implementations are being used in Lean4. In the future (that is perhaps not so distant from us) when Lean might have an ecosystem of packages that link against C code, whether it's proprietary drivers or some optimized C computation or just plain malware - feels like it'd be useful to audit a Lean constant as far into its trust boundaries as possible?
